hooks.command: guard="${CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR:-.}/.claude/hooks/claude-build-lock-guard.py"; if command -v python >/dev/null 2>&1; then python "$guard"; elif command -v python3 >/dev/null 2>&1; then python3 "$guard"; else payload=$(cat); case "$payload" in *build-lock.ps1*|*OLO_BUILD_LOCK_BYPASS*) : ;; *'cmake --build'*|*ninja*|*msbuild*|*MSBuild*) printf '%s' '{"hookSpecificOutput":{"hookEventName":"PreToolUse","permissionDecision":"deny","permissionDecisionReason":"Blocked: Python is unavailable, so the build-lock guard cannot classify this command and fails CLOSED rather than letting an unlocked build through. Route the build through .claude/skills/run-oloengine/build-lock.ps1, install Python, or add the literal marker OLO_BUILD_LOCK_BYPASS if this is not a build."}}' ;; esac; fi

hooks="${CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR:-.}/.claude/hooks"; if command -v pwsh >/dev/null 2>&1; then pwsh -NoProfile -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File "$hooks/claude-stop-hook.ps1"; else sh "$hooks/claude-stop-hook.sh"; fi

_comment: Shared Claude Code project settings. Per-user permissions live in settings.local.json (gitignored). Per-user state lives elsewhere in .claude/ (also gitignored). NOTE: builds go through .claude/skills/run-oloengine/build-lock.ps1, the cross-worktree mutex (one Debug build peaks at ~47 GiB of 64). That is enforced by the PreToolUse hook above, not by a permission rule — a deny rule degrades to a prompt, which an unattended session in auto mode approves. Escape hatch for a command that only mentions a build tool: the literal marker OLO_BUILD_LOCK_BYPASS.
